decisions.detail: QUOTE: **Default (`MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` not defined):** `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` expands to `private_x`. ... **Opt-out (`MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` defined):** `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` expands to `x`, and the field has its real name. | WHY: The answer states both the default rename to private_<member> and the unchanged expansion when MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS is defined.

decisions.mark: explains that the two branches give different consumers different views — code that defines MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS sees plain member names while an ordinary consumer of the public headers sees the renamed ones
decisions.detail: QUOTE: Default (`MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` not defined): `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` expands to `private_x`... Opt-out (`MBEDTLS_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ACCESS` defined): `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` expands to `x`... in these translation units `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` is just `x`, so `ctx.x` compiles | WHY: The answer says that code defining the opt-out sees plain member names, and that ordinary code sees `private_x` names. It also says the escape hatch gives `bar.private_foo` in user code.

decisions.mark: concludes that this enforces API opacity at COMPILE time by breaking the member name, rather than by hiding the struct layout — the fields remain visible and sized
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "`MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(x)` expands to `private_x`. A field declared as `MBEDTLS_PRIVATE(nr)` is really named `private_nr`, so `ctx.nr` fails to compile." | WHY: The answer says the macro renames the member so access fails at compile time. It never says the struct layout stays visible and sized, but the compile-time rename mechanism it describes is the substance of the item.
